svg.text:
Drag and drop the labels from the word bank to the correct target slots on the flower diagram.
Each label describes a specific part of flower anatomy. Match all 10 labels correctly to complete the activity.
Flower parts are essential for plant reproduction: • Petals attract pollinators • Stamens produce pollen • Pistil receives pollen • Sepals protect the bud

g.text:
Key Flower Anatomy Terms:
• Petal - Colorful part that attracts pollinators • Sepal - Green leaf-like structures protecting the bud • Stamen - Male reproductive organ (anther + filament) • Pistil - Female reproductive organ (stigma + style + ovary) • Anther - Pollen-producing part of stamen • Filament - Stalk supporting the anther • Ovary - Contains ovules, becomes fruit after fertilization • Style - Connects stigma to ovary • Stigma - Receives pollen during pollination • Receptacle - Base where flower parts attach
Tip: Start with the larger structures (petal, sepal, stamen, pistil) before moving to the smaller, detailed parts.

1. Petal → Colorful outer part of flower 2. Sepal → Green protective leaves at base 3. Stamen → Male reproductive organ (anther + filament) 4. Pistil → Female reproductive organ 5. Anther → Produces pollen grains 6. Filament → Supports the anther 7. Ovary → Contains ovules, develops into fruit 8. Style → Connects stigma to ovary 9. Stigma → Receives pollen 10. Receptacle → Base where all parts attach
✓ All labels placed correctly! Great job!

Clicking reset will: • Clear all placed labels from target slots • Return all labels to the word bank • Reset your progress • Allow you to start the activity fresh
This is useful if you want to: - Practice the activity again - Start over with a different approach - Test your knowledge from scratch - Clear incorrect placements
